explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/289 with the reported positive resolution (LEAP formal proof linked). For all large k there are k pairwise separated (non-overlapping, non-adjacent) intervals, each of length ≥ 2, whose reciprocal sums total 1. An interval starting at 0 (with 0⁻¹ = 0 in ℚ) could only act like {1} via [0,1], which cannot be part of a k ≥ 2 solution, since the other intervals contribute positively. So the junk value does not trivialise the statement.
